name: Verified Accelerator Hardware at Scale
description: Accelerators whose design, fabrication and assembly can be verified by the buyer: trusted-foundry production, split manufacturing, imaging-based comparison against a golden design and tamper-resistant packaging, at the volumes a frontier training cluster needs.

current_state.summary: Trusted-foundry programmes exist for low-volume defence parts; nothing comparable exists for leading-edge accelerators at cluster scale.

technical_feasibility.notes: Leading-edge fabs are few and abroad; verification of a 100-billion-transistor die is unsolved.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: A fab and verification programme measured in years.

cost.notes: Trusted fab capacity, verification tooling, packaging; illustrative.

supply_scarcity.notes: Fixed by a handful of fabs.

organizational_readiness.notes: Labs cannot build this; they can only fund and buy it.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without verifiable hardware, a state that controls part of the fab or assembly chain can ship an implant no downstream inspection finds.

open_questions.question: Can a leading-edge die be verified against its design at all?
open_questions.impact_if_resolved_negatively: The supply-chain approach stays open at OC5.

future_note: FUTURE CAPABILITY, authored assumption: this does not exist today at the scale described. It is counted only when the 'future capabilities' world toggle is on, and its cost, lead time and effect are illustrative R&D estimates, not measurements.

counters.why: Buyer-verifiable fabrication and assembly removes the implant-at-the-factory path for accelerators.
Tamper-resistant, verified packaging defeats the probing that ordinary chip tamper protection only detects.
Covers the hardware half of an ML supply-chain compromise, not the software half.
Verified designs can be checked for deliberate emanation channels.
Verified on-die memory protection makes hardware in hand harder to read.

name: Government-Cleared Workforce with State Counter-Intelligence
description: Everyone with access to the weights holds a government clearance, and a state counter-intelligence service actively protects the programme: vetting, reinvestigation, monitoring of foreign approaches and offensive counter-intelligence against recruiters.

current_state.summary: Clearances exist for defence contractors; no AI lab's weight-access workforce is cleared, and no state counter-intelligence service has taken on a lab as a protected programme.

technical_feasibility.notes: The machinery exists for defence programmes; applying it to a private lab is a policy decision.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Clearance backlogs and the legal basis for a protected private programme.

cost.notes: Cleared staffing premium, facilities for cleared work, liaison; illustrative.

supply_scarcity.notes: Government backlogs measured in months to years.

organizational_readiness.notes: Much of the research workforce could not be cleared.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without state counter-intelligence, a lab faces a foreign intelligence service's recruiters with HR and an insider-risk team.

future_note: FUTURE CAPABILITY, authored assumption: this does not exist today at the scale described. It is counted only when the 'future capabilities' world toggle is on, and its cost, lead time and effect are illustrative R&D estimates, not measurements.

counters.why: State counter-intelligence detects and disrupts recruitment that HR-grade vetting misses.
Cleared, state-protected access cannot be approved around by the organisation alone.
Vendors with access must hold clearances too.
Counter-intelligence support for coerced staff.
Clearance investigation of new hires.
State review of influence over the programme.
Fewer people hold standing access, and those who do are reinvestigated.

name: Formally Verified Weight-Access Stack
description: The software that stands between an attacker and the weights - separation kernel, key-release service, serving interface and the cross-domain guard on the air gap - is small enough to be, and is, formally verified end to end, with verified compilation and hardware models.

current_state.summary: Verified components exist (seL4, CompCert, verified cross-domain guards in defence); an end-to-end verified weight-access stack does not.

technical_feasibility.notes: Each piece has been verified somewhere; the composition at this scale has not.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Proof engineering at a scale never attempted.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without verification, every access-control and guard component is one memory-safety bug away from a path the attacker did not have to earn.

future_note: FUTURE CAPABILITY, authored assumption: this does not exist today at the scale described. It is counted only when the 'future capabilities' world toggle is on, and its cost, lead time and effect are illustrative R&D estimates, not measurements.

counters.why: A verified cross-domain guard is the residual counter for bridging the air gap.
A verified multi-party key-release policy means no one person holds standing access to read the weights.
Verified code removes the access-control software bugs that assurance only reduces.
Verified protocol implementations close implementation flaws, not design flaws.
The weight-access path no longer runs general-purpose ML stack code.
Policy is part of the verified artefact, so misconfiguration is caught by proof.
No ambient privilege in the verified stack to escalate through.
The confinement boundary is verified rather than hardened.

name: Sovereign Protected Facility
description: The weights live in a government-protected site with a state guard force, airspace and perimeter protection, and the legal standing of a national-security facility, so that armed seizure and military takeover meet the state, not a contract guard company.

current_state.summary: National laboratories and some defence sites have this protection; no AI lab's weights do.

technical_feasibility.notes: Proven for national labs; a policy decision to extend it.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Site selection, construction and the legal basis.

cost.notes: Site, construction, guard force; illustrative, partly state-funded.

vendor_dependency.notes: Only a state can provide the guard force and legal standing.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: Secure sites with grid power at training scale

organizational_readiness.notes: Moves the lab's crown jewels onto state ground.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without state protection, an adversary willing to use force meets a fence and a private guard contract.

future_note: FUTURE CAPABILITY, authored assumption: this does not exist today at the scale described. It is counted only when the 'future capabilities' world toggle is on, and its cost, lead time and effect are illustrative R&D estimates, not measurements.

counters.why: Only a state can meet a military takeover; a sovereign site makes that the defender.
A state guard force and layered perimeter is the residual counter for evading access control.
Armed response measured in minutes, by a state force rather than a contract guard company.
Fewer people ever reach the floor.
Links stay on protected ground.
Emanation and RF protection at state grade.

name: Trustworthy AI Monitors
description: Monitoring of the lab's own models by systems whose trustworthiness is established, not assumed: interpretability-based checks of what a model is doing, and monitors verified not to collude, so that manipulation of operators, covert channels and self-distillation are caught as reliably as overt copying.

current_state.summary: Interpretability and AI-control research are active, but no monitor's trustworthiness can be established today.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Depends on research breakthroughs; the range is a guess.

cost.notes: Research programme and monitoring compute; illustrative.

organizational_readiness.notes: Nobody knows if it can be built.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without trustworthy monitors, the lab watches a capable model with tools that model may understand better than its operators do.

future_note: FUTURE CAPABILITY, authored assumption: this does not exist today at the scale described. It is counted only when the 'future capabilities' world toggle is on, and its cost, lead time and effect are illustrative R&D estimates, not measurements.

counters.why: Requests a model makes of staff are checked by a monitor that can be trusted not to share its goals.
Self-distillation into permitted outputs is detected by what the model is doing, not by volume.
Covert channels in outputs are visible to an interpretability-based check.
Sabotage of code and evaluations is caught by monitors that do not collude.
Adds a trusted check on staging of weight copies.
Adds a trusted check on credential and tool misuse.
Adds a trusted check on unsanctioned jobs.
Adds a trusted check on escape attempts.
